description: Install Three.js + React Three Fiber + Drei, then build the complete 3D Personal Health Twin frontend feature: OrganViewer3D, OrganInfoPanel, HealthTimeline, HealthChangeExplorer, MedicationSafetyPanel, and DigitalTwin main page. Finally update App.jsx to add the /digital-twin route (Patient-only) and nav items. This feature depends on FEAT-001 completing first (because FEAT-001 cleans up App.jsx garden refs before we modify App.jsx here).
steps: STEP 1 — Install 3D libraries: Run in frontend/: npm install three @react-three/fiber @react-three/drei --save --legacy-peer-deps. Verify npm run build passes after install.

STEP 3 — Create frontend/src/pages/digital-twin/OrganViewer3D.jsx: - Imports: Canvas from @react-three/fiber; OrbitControls, Html from @react-three/drei; useRef, useState, Suspense from react; * as THREE from three. - ORGAN_CONFIGS array (5 entries with id, label, geometry args, color, position, scale): heart: { id:'heart', label:'Heart', geometry:, color:'#e63946', position:[0,0,0], scale:[0.55,0.55,0.55] } lungs: two meshes — leftLung { id:'leftLung', label:'Left Lung', geometry:, color:'#ffb3c1', opacity:0.85, position:[-0.85,0,0], scale:[0.6,0.85,0.6] }, rightLung similar at [0.85,0,0] liver: { id:'liver', label:'Liver', geometry:, color:'#8B4513', position:[0.3,-0.9,0], scale:[1.1,0.5,0.8] } kidneys: two CapsuleGeometry — leftKidney { id:'leftKidney', label:'Left Kidney', geometry:, color:'#9b2226', position:[-0.95,-0.5,0], scale:[1,1,1] }, rightKidney at [0.95,-0.5,0] brain: { id:'brain', label:'Brain', geometry:, color:'#adb5bd', position:[0,1.1,0], scale:[1,0.75,1.1] } - For multi-mesh organs (lungs, kidneys), group them and treat as one organ id ('lungs', 'kidneys'). - Each mesh uses with color, emissive='#ffffff', emissiveIntensity={selectedOrgan===id ? 0.25 : 0}. Lungs use transparent=true opacity=0.85. - Organ click: onClick={() => onOrganSelect(id)}. - floating label: position above mesh, small text, className 'organ-label', hidden when selectedOrgan !== null && selectedOrgan !== id. - OrbitControls ref: const controlsRef = useRef(); . Camera reset button as HTML overlay (absolute top-right of canvas wrapper div): . - Canvas props: camera={{ position:[0,0,4], fov:50 }}, style={{ height:'100%', width:'100%' }}. Ambient light intensity 0.6, directional light position [5,5,5]. - Outer wrapper: position:relative, height inherited from parent. - Below canvas: disclaimer

text: '⚠️ Illustrative anatomical models — not medically accurate representations. For educational purposes only.' in muted monospace small text. - Props interface: { selectedOrgan: string|null, onOrganSelect: (id:string)=>void, patientData: object }

STEP 4 — Create frontend/src/pages/digital-twin/OrganInfoPanel.jsx:
  - Props: { selectedOrgan, patientData }.
  - ORGAN_INFO map: { heart: { name:'Heart', description:'The heart pumps oxygenated blood throughout the body via a continuous rhythmic contraction cycle.', biomarkerKeys:['cholesterol','ldl','hdl','triglycerides','systolic','diastolic','total cholesterol'], predictionType:'Heart Attack' }, lungs: { name:'Lungs', description:'The lungs facilitate gas exchange, supplying oxygen to the blood and removing carbon dioxide.', biomarkerKeys:['oxygen saturation','spo2','peak flow','fev1'], predictionType:null }, liver: { name:'Liver', description:'The liver metabolises nutrients, detoxifies chemicals, and produces essential proteins.', biomarkerKeys:['alt','ast','bilirubin','ggt','albumin','sgpt','sgot'], predictionType:null }, kidneys: { name:'Kidneys', description:'The kidneys filter waste from the blood and regulate fluid and electrolyte balance.', biomarkerKeys:['creatinine','urea','bun','egfr','uric acid'], predictionType:null }, brain: { name:'Brain', description:'The brain coordinates sensory input, motor output, cognition, and autonomic functions.', biomarkerKeys:[], predictionType:null } }.
  - Biomarker extraction: for each report in patientData.pathology, parse report_data array, for each item check if name.toLowerCase() includes any biomarkerKey. Collect matches with value, unit, and parent report created_at as date.
  - Risk extraction: find prediction in patientData.predictions where disease_type === info.predictionType; take the most recent one (first after sort by created_at desc).
  - Render: glass-card with organ name heading, description paragraph, biomarkers table (name | value | unit | date), risk score badge, link to /profile?tab=vault.
  - Empty state (no selectedOrgan): 'Select an organ above to view health information.'
  - Empty data state (organ selected but no data): 'No recorded data for this organ yet...'
  - Do not display any values not present in the API response.

STEP 5 — Create frontend/src/pages/digital-twin/HealthTimeline.jsx:
  - Props: { patientData, loading }.
  - Flatten patientData.predictions (add _type:'prediction', _title: item.disease_type, _summary: item.risk_score+'% '+item.risk_level), patientData.pathology (add _type:'pathology', _title:'Pathology Report', _summary: report_data.length+' biomarkers'), patientData.prescriptions (add _type:'prescription', _title:'Prescription', _summary: extracted_data.medicines?.length+' medication(s)') into one array.
  - Sort by created_at descending. Slice to 20.
  - Vertical timeline: left border line, each item is a card offset to the right with a coloured dot. Colors: prediction=#ff8c00, pathology=#00f5d4, prescription=#df40ff.
  - Expandable: clicking an item toggles expanded state (expandedId state). Expanded shows full details (prediction: risk_score, risk_level, clinical_reasoning; pathology: all biomarkers list; prescription: medicines list).
  - Loading: spinner. Empty: empty state message.
  - Link each item to /profile?tab=vault.

STEP 6 — Create frontend/src/pages/digital-twin/HealthChangeExplorer.jsx:
  - Props: { patientData }.
  - Build biomarker list: flatten all patientData.pathology report_data arrays into a list of { name, value, unit, date (from parent created_at), reference_range (if present) }. Deduplicate by name keeping most recent.
  - State: selectedBiomarker (object|null), hypotheticalValue (string, raw input), inputError (string).
  - Dropdown (select element) listing biomarker names. On change: set selectedBiomarker.
  - Hypothetical input: type=number, min=0, max=10000, labelled 'Hypothetical Value (not saved)'. On change: validate (must be a number between 0 and 10000); set inputError if invalid.
  - Comparison section (only when both selectedBiomarker and valid hypotheticalValue): show recorded value vs hypothetical value side by side; absolute diff and % change; horizontal bar SVG or div showing proportion; plain-language sentence (e.g. 'Your hypothetical value of X is Y units higher than your recorded value of Z.').
  - Reference range section: only shown if selectedBiomarker.reference_range exists. Show range, indicate if recorded/hypothetical fall within it (simple text: Within range / Outside range).
  - Disclaimer banner: fixed at top of component, amber background, text: 'This is an educational comparison tool only. Hypothetical values are never saved to your records.'
  - Empty state if no pathology data.
  - NO backend calls.

STEP 7 — Create frontend/src/pages/digital-twin/MedicationSafetyPanel.jsx:
  - Props: { patientData }.
  - Extract current medications: iterate patientData.prescriptions, for each parse extracted_data.medicines array; collect { name, dosage }; deduplicate by name (case-insensitive); take up to 10.
  - State: safetyReport (null), loading (bool), error (string), hasRun (bool).
  - Allergy cross-check (client-side only for display): check if any medication name includes any of patientData.profile.allergies strings (case-insensitive). Store allergyHits array.
  - Display: list current medications (name + dosage or 'As directed'). List known allergies from profile.allergies. Allergy hits shown in red alert box (client-side check).
  - 'Run Safety Check' button: POST /api/telemetry/drug-safety/ with { medications: currentMeds }. On success set safetyReport and hasRun=true.
  - Result display:
    Grey: no meds → 'No medications on record to check.'
    Green: hasRun && !safetyReport.has_interactions && safetyReport.critical_warnings.length===0 → 'No known interactions detected.' in green.
    Orange: safetyReport.critical_warnings.length > 0 → list each warning in amber.
    safetyReport.dietary_precautions (if present) → show in a separate list.
    safetyReport.side_effects (if present) → show in a separate list.
    safetyReport.summary (if present) → show in a collapsed <details> 'Full Clinical Summary'.
  - Footer: 'Drug safety information is provided for awareness only. Always consult your prescribing physician.'
  - Do not add any local interaction logic (no INTERACTIONS array usage). All logic is in backend endpoint.

STEP 8 — Create frontend/src/pages/DigitalTwin.jsx: - const OrganViewer3D = React.lazy(() => import('./digital-twin/OrganViewer3D')). - Import (non-lazy): OrganInfoPanel, HealthTimeline, HealthChangeExplorer, MedicationSafetyPanel. - Import: Cpu, Activity, Shield, Zap, Brain icons from lucide-react. - State: selectedOrgan='heart', patientData={profile:null,predictions:[],pathology:[],prescriptions:[]}, loading=true, error='', activeTab='timeline'. - On mount useEffect: try api.get('/health-twin/') → map response to patientData (profile=data.profile, predictions=data.predictions, pathology=data.pathology_reports, prescriptions=data.prescriptions). Catch: fall back to Promise.all([api.get('/telemetry/emergency/'), api.get('/predictions/'), api.get('/pathology/'), api.get('/prescriptions/')]) → map responses to patientData. Set loading=false in finally. - Sidebar injection: useEffect → setSidebarContent(
...
) with: heading 'Personal Health Twin', patient name + blood group from patientData.profile (if loaded), 5 organ buttons (each sets selectedOrgan state). Cleanup return () => setSidebarContent(null). - Layout: div with className='reveal px-1 theme-general' (matches rest of app). - Page header: h2 'Personal Health Twin' with Cpu icon, subtitle 'Your medical data in an interactive 3D view.' - Two-column Bootstrap row: col-lg-7 and col-lg-5. - Left col (col-lg-7): 3D viewer container div style={{height:'480px',position:'relative'}} wrapping }>. Below viewer: . - Right col (col-lg-5): tab buttons row (Timeline | Safety | Explorer | About), then tab content panel. - Timeline tab: - Safety tab: - Explorer tab: - About tab: static text describing the feature, its limitations, noting models are illustrative. - Loading state: centered spinner. - Error state: error message + retry button that calls fetchData again. - Uses useContext(SidebarContext) for setSidebarContent. - Props: { user }.

STEP 9 — Update frontend/src/App.jsx:
  (a) Add 'import DigitalTwin from ./pages/DigitalTwin' in imports block.
  (b) Add 'Cpu' to the lucide-react import line.
  (c) In isSidebarPage const, add '|| location.pathname.includes(digital-twin)'.
  (d) In <Routes>, add: <Route path='/digital-twin' element={user && user.role === 'Patient' ? <DigitalTwin user={user} /> : <Navigate to='/auth' />} />
  (e) In desktop Patient nav block, add <NavLink to='/digital-twin' icon={<Cpu size={16}/>} label='Health Twin'/> after the Diet nav item.
  (f) In mobile Patient nav block, add <MobileNavLink to='/digital-twin' label='Personal Health Twin' onClick={() => setIsOpen(false)}/> after Diet item.

STEP 10 — Update frontend/src/services/api.js:
  In the 401 interceptor path exclusion block (the list that checks window.location.pathname), add '/digital-twin' alongside '/diet' so that 401 responses on the health twin page do not trigger an unwanted redirect while the user is already authenticated.
acceptance_criteria: npm run build in frontend/ exits 0 with no errors after all files are created.
Route /digital-twin is accessible to Patient users and redirects Guests/Doctors to /auth.
'Health Twin' nav item appears for Patient users in desktop and mobile nav.
The 3D viewer renders 5 procedural organ shapes (heart, lungs, liver, kidneys, brain) in the Canvas.
Clicking an organ in the viewer updates the selected organ and shows info in OrganInfoPanel.
The HealthTimeline renders up to 20 records sorted newest first, with expandable items.
HealthChangeExplorer shows a dropdown of biomarker names from pathology data; entering a hypothetical value shows comparison and never triggers any API call.
MedicationSafetyPanel lists medications from prescriptions and has a 'Run Safety Check' button that calls POST /api/telemetry/drug-safety/.
The 3D canvas is lazy-loaded via React.lazy (does not block initial page render).
Disclaimer text is visible on OrganViewer3D and HealthChangeExplorer.
No reference to Garden in any nav or route.
findings: Installed three, @react-three/fiber, @react-three/drei with --legacy-peer-deps. Created frontend/src/pages/digital-twin/ directory with OrganViewer3D.jsx (5 procedural organs, OrbitControls, Html labels, Reset View button, illustrative disclaimer), OrganInfoPanel.jsx (biomarker extraction from pathology, risk score badge, vault link), HealthTimeline.jsx (flattened records, expandable cards, color-coded by type), HealthChangeExplorer.jsx (dropdown of biomarkers, hypothetical input, bar visualization, plain-language diff, reference range check, disclaimer banner, NO backend calls), MedicationSafetyPanel.jsx (medication extraction, allergy cross-check, POST /api/telemetry/drug-safety/, full result display). Created frontend/src/pages/DigitalTwin.jsx (React.lazy OrganViewer3D, Suspense fallback, SidebarContext injection with organ buttons, two-column layout, tab UI for Timeline/Safety/Explorer/About, fallback API chain). Updated App.jsx: added Cpu icon import, DigitalTwin import, 'digital-twin' to isSidebarPage, /digital-twin Patient-only route, desktop and mobile nav items. Updated api.js: added '/digital-twin' to 401 interceptor exclusion. npm run build exits 0 (2764 modules transformed). OrganViewer3D lazy-splits to its own chunk as expected.
